subject: phy
title: Kinetic Theory of Gases
syllabus: Equation of state of a perfect gas, work done on compressing a gas. Kinetic theory of gases — assumptions, the concept of pressure. Kinetic interpretation of temperature: RMS speed of gas molecules; degrees of freedom, law of equipartition of energy, applications to specific heat capacities of gases; mean free path, Avogadro's number.

body: PV = nRT = Nk_{B}T, ρ = \f{PM}{RT}, R = 8.314 J mol^{−1} K^{−1}, k_{B} = 1.38 × 10^{−23} J/K
Fixed V: P ∝ T (so \f{ΔP}{P} = \f{ΔT}{T}); fixed P: V ∝ T; fixed T: P ∝ \f{1}{V}.
Joining two vessels: moles add — \f{P_{1}V_{1}}{T_{1}} + \f{P_{2}V_{2}}{T_{2}} = \f{P(V_{1} + V_{2})}{T}.
Graphs: on P–T the slope ∝ density; on V–T the slope ∝ \f{1}{P}.

body: Average KE depends ONLY on T (not on the gas). Speeds depend on T and M: v ∝ √{\f{T}{M}}.
v_{rms} > v_{avg} > v_{mp} (√{3} : √{8/π} : √{2}). \overline{v^{2}} ∝ T is a straight line.
Internal energy of air in a room = \f{5}{2}PV — it does not change when you heat the room at fixed P!

check.q: v_rms of H₂ is 2 km/s. v_rms of O₂ at the same T :

body: ½k_{B}T per degree of freedom; C_{v} = \f{f}{2}R, C_{p} = (\f{f}{2} + 1)R, γ = 1 + \f{2}{f}
Monoatomic f = 3; rigid diatomic 5; non-linear (CH_{4}, NH_{3}) 6 (3 translation + 3 rotation). Each vibrational mode adds 2.
Mixtures: C_{v,mix} = \f{Σn_{i}C_{v,i}}{Σn_{i}}; then γ_{mix} = \f{C_{v} + R}{C_{v}} (NOT the average of the γs). Mixing gases conserves total U.

check.q: γ for a gas with f = 6 :

body: λ ∝ \f{1}{d^{2}} and ∝ \f{1}{n}; at fixed n it does not depend on T.
Thin gas (low P) → long free paths.

check.q: Molecular diameter doubled, same n. λ becomes :

traps: Average KE depends only on T — the same for H₂ and O₂ at the same T; their speeds differ.
γ of a mixture: average C_{v} first, never the γs.
Use M in kg/mol in v_{rms} = √{3RT/M}.
Per molecule use k_{B}; per mole use R.

steps.note: KE, speeds and mean free path
Degrees of freedom, C_{v}, γ and mixtures

pyq.q: Two moles a monoatomic gas is mixed with six moles of a diatomic gas. The molar specific heat of the mixture at constant volume is :
If three moles of monoatomic gas (γ = \f{5}{3}) is mixed with two moles of a diatomic gas (γ = \f{7}{5}), the value of adiabatic exponent γ for the mixture is:
N moles of a polyatomic gas (f = 6) must be mixed with two moles of a monoatomic gas so that the mixture behaves as a diatomic gas. The value of N is :
A gas mixture consists of 8 moles of argon and 6 moles of oxygen at temperature T. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system is
If 2 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas at temperature T, is mixed with 6 mole of another ideal monoatomic gas at temperature 2T then the temperature of mixture is :
sol: No heat lost: internal energy is shared. Same C_{v} → T = \f{n_{1}T_{1} + n_{2}T_{2}}{n_{1} + n_{2}}.

pyq.q: A mixture of one mole of monoatomic gas and one mole of a diatomic gas (rigid) are kept at room temperature (27 °C). The ratio of specific heat of gases at constant volume respectively is:

γ_{A} is the specific heat ratio of monoatomic gas A having 3 translational degrees of freedom. γ_{B} is the specific heat ratio of polyatomic gas B having 3 translational, 3 rotational degrees of freedom and 1 vibrational mode. If \f{γ_{A}}{γ_{B}} = (1 + \f{1}{n}), then the value of n is ____
sol: A vibrational mode counts twice (kinetic + potential): f_{B} = 3 + 3 + 2 = 8.

pyq.q: The translational degrees of freedom (f_{t}) and rotational degrees of freedom (f_{r}) of CH_{4} molecule are :
sol: Every molecule moves in 3 directions: f_{t} = 3.
CH_{4} is non-linear (tetrahedral): it can spin about 3 axes → f_{r} = 3.

pyq.q: Energy of 10 non rigid diatomic molecules at temperature T is :
sol: Non-rigid diatomic: 3 translation + 2 rotation + 2 (one vibration) = 7 → \f{7}{2}k_{B}T per molecule.
10 molecules → 35 k_{B}T (molecules, so k_{B}, not R).

pyq.q: For a diatomic gas, if γ_{1} = (\f{C_{p}}{C_{v}}) for rigid molecules and γ_{2} = (\f{C_{p}}{C_{v}}) for another diatomic molecules, but also having vibrational modes. Then, which one of the following options is correct? (C_{p} and C_{v} are specific heats of the gas at constant pressure and volume)
sol: γ = 1 + \f{2}{f}: more degrees of freedom → smaller γ.
Rigid f = 5 (γ = 1.4); with vibration f = 7 (γ ≈ 1.29) → γ_{2} < γ_{1}.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Change in internal energy of a system containing n mole of ideal gas can be written as ΔU = nC_{v}(T_{f} − T_{i}) = \f{nR}{γ − 1}(T_{f} − T_{i}), where γ = \f{C_{p}}{C_{v}}, T_{i} = initial temperature, T_{f} = final temperature. Statement II: Relation between degree of freedom f and γ (= C_{p}/C_{v}) is (γ = 1 + \f{2}{f}). Choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: C_{v} = \f{R}{γ − 1} for any ideal gas → true.
II: C_{v} = \f{f}{2}R → γ = 1 + \f{2}{f} → true. But I follows from C_{p} − C_{v} = R, not from II.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

pyq.q: If the root mean square velocity of hydrogen molecule at a given temperature and pressure is 2 km/s, the root mean square velocity of oxygen at the same condition in km/s is :
A sample contains mixture of helium and oxygen gas. The ratio of root mean square speed of helium and oxygen in the sample, is :
The average kinetic energy of a monatomic molecule is 0.414 eV at temperature : (Use k_{B} = 1.38 × 10^{−23} J/mol-K)
For a particular ideal gas which of the following graphs represents the variation of mean squared velocity of the gas molecules with temperature?
sol: A straight line through the origin.
o: A curve rising steeply at first and then flattening
A curve rising slowly at first and then more and more steeply
A curve that rises to a peak and then falls
A straight line through the origin

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: If the average kinetic energy of H_{2} and O_{2} molecules, kept in two different sized containers, are same, then their temperatures will be same. Reason R: The r.m.s. speed of H_{2} and O_{2} molecules are same at same temperature. Choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Average KE (translational) = \f{3}{2}k_{B}T depends only on T → A true.
v_{rms} = √{\f{3RT}{M}} differs (H_{2} is 4 times faster) → R false.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

pyq.q: The internal energy of air in 4 m × 4 m × 3 m sized room at 1 atmospheric pressure will be ____ × 10^{6} J. (Consider air as diatomic molecule)

A cylindrical tube AB of length l, closed at both ends contains an ideal gas of 1 mol having molecular weight M. The tube is rotated in a horizontal plane with constant angular velocity ω about an axis perpendicular to AB and passing through the edge at end A. If P_{A} and P_{B} are the pressures at A and B respectively, then (Consider the temperature is same at all points in the tube)
sol: A slice at distance r needs a net inward force: dP = ρω^{2}r dr with ρ = \f{PM}{RT}.

pyq.q: Pressure of an ideal gas, contained in a closed vessel, is increased by 0.4% when heated by 1 °C. Its initial temperature must be:

There are two vessels filled with an ideal gas where volume of one is double the volume of other. The large vessel contains the gas at 8 kPa at 1000 K while the smaller vessel contains the gas at 7 kPa at 500 K. If the vessels are connected to each other by a thin tube allowing the gas to flow and the temperature of both vessels is maintained at 600 K, at steady state the pressure in the vessels will be (in kPa).

A mixture of carbon dioxide and oxygen has volume 8310 cm^{3}, temperature 300 K, pressure 100 kPa and mass 13.2 g. The number of moles of carbon dioxide and oxygen gases in the mixture respectively are _______ . (Assume both carbon dioxide and oxygen gases behave like ideal gases) [R = 8.31 J/mol. K]

P-T diagram of an ideal gas having three different densities ρ_{1}, ρ_{2}, ρ_{3} (in three different cases) is shown: all three are straight lines through the origin, ρ_{1} the steepest, then ρ_{2}, then ρ_{3}. Which of the following is correct :
sol: Steepest line → largest density: ρ_{1} > ρ_{2} > ρ_{3}.

pyq.q: Two isobaric processes for the same mass of an ideal gas are drawn as straight lines through the origin on a V–T graph; the line labelled P_{2} is steeper than the line labelled P_{1}. Then
sol: Steeper line → smaller pressure → P_{1} > P_{2}.

pyq.q: An ideal gas at pressure P and temperature T is expanding such that PT^{3} = constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is ____.
If n is the number density and d is the diameter of the molecule, then the average distance covered by a molecule between two successive collisions (i.e. mean free path) is represented by :
sol: A molecule sweeps a cylinder of cross-section πd^{2}; relative motion adds √{2}.

pyq.q: The mean free path of a molecule of diameter 5 × 10^{−10} m at the temperature 41 °C and pressure 1.38 × 10^{5} Pa, is given as ____ m. (Given k_{B} = 1.38 × 10^{−23} J/K).
The mean free path and the average speed of oxygen molecules at 300 K and 1 atm are 3 × 10^{−7} m and 600 m/s, respectively. Find the frequency of its collisions.
sol: Collisions per second = \f{average speed}{mean free path}.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : The mean free path of gas molecules is inversely proportional to square of molecular diameter. Statement (II) : Average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to absolute temperature of gas. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below:
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
